campaign: Deliver multimodal Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS and meet native Strata performance

items.title: A driver start takes the campaign lock before it reads a running worker's record, and one fixture holds what a start admits

budget.reason: Estimate before the survey: the noteUncleanEnd call moves below processcontrol.BeginCampaign in cmd/loop/main.go run; the fixture step changes test code alone.

steps.title: run reads the running record only after BeginCampaign succeeds, so a refused second start leaves the record and the unclean log untouched
steps.rationale:
SQA-338: cmd/loop/main.go run calls noteUncleanEnd before processcontrol.BeginCampaign, so a second driver started beside one whose worker runs logs that live run as unclean in driver_unclean.log and removes driver_running.json, and only then is refused by loop_supervisor.lock; the startup task's IgnoreNew covers its own instances, not a direct start.

noteUncleanEnd moves after a successful BeginCampaign, under its deferred release; a genuine orphan is still logged and cleared by the next admitted start, as TestTheStartupTaskRunsTheDriverAtBoot holds.

Serves: setup-steps; a refused start never erases a working run's recovery record.
Disappears: recovery state changed before admission.
Evidence: with a campaign held and a running record kept, a second start is refused and the record and the unclean log keep their bytes.
Batch: host lane.

steps.title: One start-admission fixture holds the default configuration, its prompt, no-clobber and the refusals, and init_config_test.go goes
steps.rationale:
SQA-338: cmd/loop/init_config_test.go TestTheDriverLandsAStepThroughItsWorker and cmd/loop/driver_start_test.go TestADriverStartsFromItsConfigAlone each build a checkout, pause at once, begin a campaign and check its name; neither runs a worker or lands a step, whatever the first's name says.

The default-write, worker-command, prompt and second -init checks join the missing-prompt, missing-budget and strategy refusals in one fixture named for start admission, and init_config_test.go with its duplicate paused setup goes; subprocess continuation and stop stay with their own tests.

Serves: setup-steps; one fixture says what a driver start admits.
Disappears: init_config_test.go and its duplicate paused-start setup.
Evidence: the merged fixture holds -init's defaults, a refused second -init, the config's name on the campaign and each malformed config refused.
Batch: host lane.

items.title: A run whose empty plan has findings to file ends waiting for them, never as a completed plan, and the waiting cases count worker runs exactly

budget.reason: Estimate before the survey: internal/loop gains a findings-waiting reason that Run ends with, and cmd/loop/improve.go CycleWorthRunning reports findings to file as that answer instead of a plain not-worth-running.

steps.title: The driver ends a run whose empty plan has findings to file as waiting for them, naming them
steps.rationale:
SQA-271: with the plan empty and open P1 or P2 findings no row names, cmd/loop/improve.go CycleWorthRunning answers not worth running, internal/loop/driver.go improve files nothing, and Run ends ReasonPlanComplete with no worker run, reporting a finished plan while work waits; internal/loop/dispatch_wait_test.go also lets each held-work case run up to one worker where 0, 1 and 0 are exact.

CycleWorthRunning reports findings to file as their own answer, and Run ends with a findings-waiting reason naming them; paused, budget and stop outcomes stay. The new test replaces TestARunThatFindsWorkWaitingSaysSo at exact counts and adds the empty plan with findings.

Serves: setup-steps; an unattended run says what it waits for.
Disappears: plan-complete reported while findings wait.
Evidence: an empty plan with findings ends findings-waiting with no measurement or worker run, and each held-work case runs exactly its workers.
Batch: host lane.

items.title: Every cycle lane that runs go test runs its tests afresh, so a real-model pass is never replayed after its model or reference bytes change

budget.reason: Estimate before the survey: -count=1 joins the models and needle-reference commands in internal/landing/lanes.go cycleLanes, and two comments stop claiming the cache replays only unchanged inputs.

steps.title: The models and needle-reference cycle lanes run go test with -count=1, as every other go test cycle lane does
steps.rationale:
SQA-315: internal/landing/lanes.go cycleLanes runs the models and needle-reference lanes without -count=1, and cmd/validate cycleSuites and acquire pass those arguments on; go test keys its cache only on inputs inside the module, so a pass that opened OVERGO_SINGLE_PASS_GGUF or the needle reference fixture through dataroot is replayed after those external bytes change.

Both commands gain -count=1, as audio and sequences have, and the cycleLanes and cycleSuites comments stop saying the cache replays only what nothing changed. The new test reads every cycle lane whose verb is test, so a lane added later is held too.

Serves: held-out-quality; a cycle's real-model evidence reads the model bytes it names.
Disappears: replayed real-model passes over changed external inputs.
Evidence: every go test cycle lane's arguments carry -count=1, and a lane without it is named.
Batch: host lane.

items.title: A held-out reading, a serving attempt and a training observation carry the verification state of the recipe and task that ran

budget.reason: Estimate before the survey: internal/modelrecipe gains one reading of a recipe's state, its own task's state and not verified unless that task's active definition is the recipe; internal/evaluation/campaign.go publishSuccess, internal/servingattempt Record and internal/trainingworkflow Observer.finish call it.

steps.title: An evaluation campaign publishes its reading under the state of its own recipe and task
steps.rationale:
SQA-283: internal/evaluation/campaign.go publishSuccess reads modelrecipe.ReadModelState for recipe.TaskInference whatever task the campaign runs and discards the returned Activation; an active speech-only model with no inference alias publishes not verified, internal/scorecard earned drops that reading from its verified row, and a candidate recipe borrows the active recipe's verified state.

modelrecipe gains one reading of a recipe's state: its own task's state, not verified unless that task's active definition is the recipe. publishSuccess uses it with campaign.identity.Recipe; store errors and legacy records stay as they are.

Serves: held-out-quality; a verified row keeps the readings its own recipe earned.
Disappears: the hard-coded inference task and a borrowed activation's state.
Evidence: through publication, a non-inference recipe with no inference alias publishes verified, and a candidate beside an active recipe not verified.
Batch: host lane.

steps.title: A serving attempt and a training observation are recorded under the state of the recipe that ran
steps.rationale:
SQA-283: internal/servingattempt/servingattempt.go Record and internal/trainingworkflow/session_observation.go Observer.finish read ReadModelState for the model and task at publication and ignore the returned Activation, so an attempt by a candidate recipe is stamped with the active recipe's state.

Both recorders use the recipe-state reading the held-out step added, with the observation's own Recipe; an attempt whose recipe is not the active one is recorded not verified, and a store that cannot say leaves the state empty, as now.

Serves: failure-rate; an attempt carries the state of the recipe that served it.
Disappears: the model-wide state stamped on another recipe's attempt.
Evidence: an attempt recorded for a candidate recipe beside a verified active one carries not verified, and one for the active recipe carries verified.
Batch: host lane.

items.title: Each E4B dataset-quality cell measured on an earlier definition is reported as owed on the definition E4B serves, so coverage never reads it as current acceptance

budget.reason: Estimate before the survey: cmd/validate/media_coverage.go collectModalityProtocols reads the model's active inference definition once and writes an owed gap, naming both definitions, for a quality cell measured on another.

steps.title: The coverage projection marks a quality cell whose definition is not its model's served one as owed there, naming both definitions
steps.rationale:
SQA-277: six E4B dataset-quality cells in docs/verification/e4b-validation.json keep recipe d6ba6736 and commit 1b7ac581, as the external adapter that measured them is not in this repository, while the 24 protocol and resource cells name the served definition; cmd/validate/media_coverage.go collectModalityProtocols gives every frozen cell one generic gap, so coverage does not say which modality-quality results are owed.

For a quality cell whose ModelDefinition is not the active inference definition, collectModalityProtocols writes a gap naming both definitions, so the six read as owed; nothing is re-run, and re-measuring them waits on the adapter.

Serves: held-out-quality; coverage says which E4B modality results hold on the served definition.
Disappears: a historical quality cell read as current acceptance.
Evidence: a fixture quality cell from an earlier definition is projected owed with both named, and one from the served definition is not.
Batch: host lane.

items.title: A finding the lead's triage defers to the next full run's record no longer holds that run back, so the run that decides it can start

budget.reason: Estimate before the survey: internal/plan/findings_fall_through.go readFindings also reads master_lead_triage, and FindingsToFile passes over a finding whose triage action is deferred.

steps.title: FindingsToFile passes over a finding whose master_lead_triage action is deferred
steps.rationale:
SQA-266: its deciding evidence, each cycle lane package's wall and peak (run-once/run-wall), comes only from the next full measurement run, and .overgo-runtime/lane_walls.json still reads {}; internal/plan/findings_fall_through.go FindingsToFile holds that run until a row names every open P1 and P2 finding, and a row filed for this one keeps the plan from emptying, so the run that would decide it never starts.

FindingsToFile reads master_lead_triage and passes over a finding whose action is deferred; it stays open, and the lead files its step from the run's record. No row is revived and no selector, cache or scheduler is added.

Serves: setup-steps; the measurement run that decides SQA-266 starts with no hand edit.
Disappears: a deferred finding holding back the run that supplies its evidence.
Evidence: a register with one open deferred P2 finding and one open untriaged P2 finding names only the untriaged one.
Batch: host lane.

items.title: A claim's test-file evidence without a named symbol binds the whole file, and the same-file reach graph that missed init goes

budget.reason: Estimate before the survey: cmd/validate/claims.go loses reachedDeclarations (423 nodes), declaredNames (100) and the _test.go branch of evidencePayload, about 546 by the finding's parse; 450 is the shrink owed, leaving margin.

steps.title: A no-symbol test-file claim binds the file's normalized bytes, so a change to its init moves the claim
steps.rationale:
SQA-316: cmd/validate/claims.go evidencePayload binds a _test.go proof with no Symbol to reachedDeclarations, a same-file graph rooted at the declarations holding proof.Contains and followed by identifier names; init is no root, so a func init assigning a variable the named test reads changes what it observes while the claim's identity stays, and reverifyClaims never reruns it.

evidencePayload uses canonicalEvidence for every proof without a Symbol; reachedDeclarations and declaredNames go, and TestAClaimBindsTheTestItNames becomes the new whole-file test. Moved claims are rebound by go run ./cmd/validate -claims -run, never by hand.

Serves: held-out-quality; a published claim stays bound to the test bytes that verified it.
Disappears: about 540 production nodes of same-file reach analysis.
Evidence: changing the fixture's init assignment from 3 to 4 moves the no-symbol test-file identity.
Batch: host lane.

items.title: The open's measured draft verdict is the one decision on whether a model drafts through its own next-token layer by default, and the kept-share refusal goes

budget.reason: Estimate before the survey: internal/inference loses observeOwnDrafts (84 nodes), its constant block (14), the two Runner tally fields and the window's call; 80 is the shrink owed.

steps.title: Default drafting through a model's own next-token layer is decided by the open's measured verdict alone
steps.rationale:
SQA-257: two rules decide default drafting through a model's own next-token layer: internal/inference/nextn_device_speculation.go observeOwnDrafts refuses it once fewer than one in ten of 48 drafts were kept, and JudgeOwnDrafts, recorded per model, build and card by internal/modelcli/draft_verdict.go, refuses it where drafting decodes slower; that file's readings show the kept share does not decide the rate, Qwen3.5-4B keeping half its drafts yet decoding 57 tok/s drafted against 95 plainly.

observeOwnDrafts, its tallies and constants and TestOwnDraftsRefusedWhereFewAreKept go; the measured verdict is the one default decision, and a request that asks to speculate still drafts.

Serves: throughput; a served model drafts by default exactly where drafting decodes faster.
Disappears: the kept-share refusal, its tallies, constants and test.
Evidence: judgeDrafts decides over recorded rates, and Runner holds no kept-share tally.
Batch: host lane.

decisions.question: The scorecard's serving cells (first-output, throughput, load-time, peak-device-memory) aggregate every attempt a recipe ever made: medians over all time, total tokens over total decode time, the highest peak ever. A landed improvement shows only as old samples are outnumbered and a peak never falls. Since delete-selection each cycle measures every serving cell once at the measured commit. Should those cells read the newest successful measured attempt instead, accepting one sample's timing noise in each cycle's moved list?
options: newest measured attempt
all-time aggregates
median of the newest few attempts
decisions.recommendation: newest measured attempt
decisions.answer: newest measured attempt

decisions.question: Held-out quality is unscored for forecast, image-embedding, image-gen, seq2seq, tabular and vqa because each needs a held-out set the store lacks. Answering authorizes exactly these downloads into the datasets root, each to be verified by hash once fetched: ETTh1 (github.com/zhouhaoyi/ETDataset, 2.6 MB, forecast); BFCL v3 simple (gorilla-llm/Berkeley-Function-Calling-Leaderboard, 0.3 MB, seq2seq); BeyondArena credit-g (TabArena/BeyondArena, 0.2 MB, tabular); TIFA v1.0 (github.com/Yushi-Hu/tifa, 10 MB, image-gen); A-OKVQA validation (HuggingFaceM4/A-OKVQA, 60 MB, vqa); Imagenette 160 px (fast.ai imagenette2-160, 100 MB, image-embedding). About 173 MB in all. The other five unscored rows (generation, projection, speech, training, video-gen) use sets already on disk and are not blocked.
options: Download all six (about 173 MB)
Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)
Download none and score only what is on disk
decisions.recommendation: Download all six (about 173 MB)
decisions.answer: Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)

It exists so media evidence acquired at the pinned runtime stays valid across an output-neutral edit. Since the cycle re-acquires every media cell at the commit it promotes, and its models lane runs the media acceptance tests against the frozen references, the evidence that gate protects is re-proved every cycle: it is the same per-cell currency check validate-currency deleted. Retire the registry, its pin and the gate-time check (about 600 lines of test code, the registry JSON and the landing's pinned-path rule), or keep it and build a one-command tool for it (row media-delta-command)?

Keep the pin and build the one-command delta tool (media-delta-command)

decisions.question: Speech, image-gen and video-gen quality cannot be scored by the model alone: pocket-tts outputs audio, the image generators pictures, Wan2.1 and Un-0 clips. Each proposal scores the output by a second local model: a speech recognizer for round-trip word error rate, a vision-language model for TIFA questions and for matching a clip to its caption. evaluate has no suite in which a generator's output is judged by another model, and a record must name both the generator's recipe, which the scorecard reads, and the judge's identity, which the score depends on. One judged-generation suite kind (the projection session already shows a video to Qwen3.8-27B) would serve all three rows and their eight models, with a new session for each judge modality.
options: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen
Score speech by its recognizer round trip only, and leave image-gen and video-gen unscored
Leave all three unscored
decisions.recommendation: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen
decisions.answer: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen

decisions.question: Held-out quality of training is scored for a recipe only by a train -objective session, which publishes a held-out verdict. Qwen2.5-0.5B trains through that route and now has its verdict (a token-prediction objective over a held-out third of the WikiText-2 articles). The other six training recipes belong to routes that prove the route rather than score text: Qwen3.5-4B and 9B hybrid-stack (a bounded observed full-stack run whose evidence is that loss descends), Wan2.1 and LiveEdit dit, Hy-Embodied mot. None of those routes holds out data or scores a model, and a token-prediction objective does not fit a diffusion or a mixture-of-transformers model. Scoring them means giving each route a held-out objective of its own (days of work each, and a 20-step proof run's held-out value says little). Which do you want?
options: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route
Give each proof route a held-out objective and score its recipe
Leave the proof-route recipes unscored
decisions.recommendation: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route
decisions.answer: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route

decisions.question: identity-carry was filed to carry an evaluation only while the code it depends on is unchanged and to delete the sampled replay. Measured 2026-10-09: 46 of the 87 newest results stand on a replay-carried result, 30 of them carried 19 or 20 times; scoring those 46 in full took 13 hours 55 minutes; the code an evaluation depends on changed on 112 of the last 300 commits and cycles lie hundreds of commits apart, so with the replay deleted every cycle scores them all again, about 14 hours more a cycle. The replay's sample is the same 32 cases every time, so a change that misses them is never seen. What should carrying do?
options: Carry under an unchanged identity, else by a replay whose sample changes each time
Carry only under an unchanged identity and score the rest in full every cycle
Leave carrying as it is

decisions.question: evaluation-chain's last step, acceptance, adds a memory ceiling and a speed target to a held-out pool's acceptance and has a confirmation refuse a candidate with no resource comparison against the base within them. Every candidate the proposer makes today is other weights of the base's shape, so it has the base's memory and speed, and no row in the plan makes another kind of candidate; a served recipe's memory and speed are already read by the scorecard and by the routing decision. When should the step be built?
options: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed
Now, ahead of such a candidate
Not at all: leave memory and speed to the scorecard and the routing decision
decisions.recommendation: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed
decisions.answer: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed

decisions.question: The video codec can now convolve a clip of about ten frames or more through NVIDIA's cuDNN. Measured beside another job on the device: a decode about a third faster, an encode about a fifth, the decoder holding 6.0 GiB where it held 9.6, and every value within one of 255 levels of what overgo's own kernels give. It does so only on a machine where cuDNN is on the search path or in the bin directory CUDA_PATH names. This machine's only copy is inside a Python environment, so it still serves by the kernels and the automated checks skip the library's tests. Installing it is yours to do: cuDNN 9 for CUDA 12, about 800 MB, from NVIDIA under NVIDIA's license. The frozen video clips are the kernels' bytes, and I would accept them again under the library afterwards. Install it here?
options: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it
Keep this machine on the kernels; the library stays for machines that have it
Take the library's path back out
decisions.recommendation: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it
decisions.answer: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it
